subject: Recap and next steps — competitive bake-off (Redwood vs peers)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anika Shah <anika@veloxhealth.com>, Mark Langston <mlangston@veloxhealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap and next steps — competitive bake-off (Redwood vs peers)

Hi Anika / Mark —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned as you run the bake-off across vendors. I tried to capture the outcomes, the decision criteria you called out, and the short tests we agreed on.

High-level pain points you shared
- Unpredictable inference latency on current provider (>300ms p95 for 512-token health summaries) causing timers to blow out in the UI.
- Unit cost spikes under load (batching not optimized for variable request sizes).
- Data residency & auditability needs (SOC 2 + regional log retention).
- Need for deterministic fallbacks during degraded capacity to avoid user-facing errors.

Decision criteria (what Velox said matters most)
1) Latency: p95 <= 150ms for 512-token summarization in our preferred region.
2) Cost: predictable unit economics and visibility per-token.
3) Observability: token-level traces and per-route cost attribution.
4) Security: VPC/private deployment option + SOC 2 evidence.
5) Quality: parity with your current baseline on clinical summarization prompts.

Bake-off tests / follow-ups we proposed
- Latency sweep (Sergio): run 50/100/500 concurrent small requests and measure p50/p95/p99 across vendors. Use your anonymized EHR prompts (sample set A).
- End-to-end quality check (Marissa + Velox): run 200 baseline prompts and evaluate with your rubric.
- Cost projection (Vivek): modeled cost for 100k tokens/day in hosted vs dedicated.
- Security checklist + SOC 2 evidence (Neha): share evidence and confirm timeline for Private deployment options.

Attachments: I attached the bakeoff-plan.xlsx (test matrix) and the Redwood questionnaire (quick answers keyed to your RFP).

Proposed timeline
- Day 0–3: exchange test data access and finalize test harness.
- Day 4–7: run latency sweep and quality batch.
- Day 8: sync (30m) to review results and decide on next steps (POC vs procurement).

Open questions for you
- Can we get a sample S3 path (or small dump) with the 200 prompts for the quality run? Prefer anonymized plaintext CSV.
- Who on your side will own cost modeling / procurement conversations? You mentioned procurement@veloxhealth.com — can you confirm a contact?

Next steps (owners)
- Sergio (Redwood): set up latency harness and scripts — ETA 48 hours.
- Vivek (Redwood): prepare hosted vs dedicated cost comparison — ETA 72 hours.
- Neha (Redwood): share SOC 2 evidence pack + Private deployment checklist.
- Anika: provide S3 link or upload sample prompts and confirm procurement contact.

Thanks — looking forward to moving quickly. I’ll send a separate internal note to align owners on timelines.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:10:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Recap and next steps — competitive bake-off (Redwood vs peers)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap — this is exactly what we needed to keep momentum. A few quick clarifications and asks from our side:

1) Data sample: I uploaded an anonymized CSV (200 prompts) to our S3 test bucket: s3://velox-tests/bakeoff/clinical-sample-a.csv. Please confirm you can access it; we'll give read-only credentials to redwood-bakeoff@velox.
2) Procurement: procurement@veloxhealth.com will be the contact; the procurement lead is Luis Ramos (l.ramos@veloxhealth.com) — I looped the shared alias above for visibility.
3) POC scope: We'd like a 2-week POC if results look promising. Primary acceptance criteria will be (a) latency targets met in our environment, (b) no regressions on summary quality per our rubric, (c) clear plan for data residency.
4) Pricing ask: can you provide an initial dedicated capacity price for a 4xGPU pool and a hosted estimate for the projected 100k tokens/day? Break out token and infrastructure costs separately.

Also attaching our RFP doc for completeness (velox_rfp_2026.pdf).

One operational note: we have an internal security chat on Monday and would appreciate the SOC 2 artifact and a short bulleted answer on how Redwood handles encryption-in-transit and at-rest for Private deployments.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Anika
Director, Applied AI | VeloxHealth
anika@veloxhealth.com

Subject: Re: Recap and next steps — competitive bake-off (Redwood vs peers)

Thanks Anika — got the S3 path and the RFP. We’ve started lining up the work; below is a more concrete plan and a proposed timeline with owners.

Access
- Sergio: please confirm you can access s3://velox-tests/bakeoff/clinical-sample-a.csv with the read-only creds once Anika shares them. If any firewall/VPC peering is required for the latency sweep, we'll coordinate next steps.

Tests and acceptance criteria (concise)
- Latency sweep (Sergio) — measure p50/p95/p99 for 512-token summarization under 1/10/50/200 concurrent streams. Acceptance: p95 <= 150ms for the 512-context samples.
- Quality batch (Marissa + Velox) — run 200 prompts, compute rubric scores, and provide diff vs your baseline. Acceptance: no >5% drop in average score.
- Smoke on Private deployment (Neha) — outline network/KMS requirements; provide SOC 2 snapshots and encryption notes.
- Cost projection (Vivek) — 4x GPU Dedicated vs hosted per-token breakdown, including expected amortized infra.

Proposed schedule (all calendar days)
- Fri (Day 1): creds & access confirmed.
- Mon–Wed (Day 2–4): run latency sweep and quality batch. Sergio will upload raw metrics and logs to the shared drive.
- Thu (Day 5): 30m sync to review results and next steps.

Open questions we still have
- Are there any PII elements in the sample data that still require an additional anonymization pass?
- For the private deployment acceptance test, do you expect a full VPC peering exercise or will synthetic traffic in our hosted environment suffice for the initial smoke?

I'll follow up separately with a draft proposal and a quick cost snapshot. If Luis or anyone on procurement wants to jump on a call this week to accelerate terms, we're ready.

Best,
Marissa

Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: Velox bake-off — owners & quick tactical notes

Team — internal only note to align on the tactical playbook. Don’t forward externally without checking.

Summary of asks from Velox
- Latency sweep with S3 sample.
- Quality run with their rubric.
- Dedicated capacity pricing for 4x GPUs + hosted comparison.
- SOC 2 artifacts + Private deployment checklist.

Tactical plan
- Sergio: spin up the latency harness (use k6 + our inference-bench docker image) and validate with the 512-token test set. Share raw p95/p99 logs in the drive folder: drive.redwood/example/bakeoff-harness/results. ETA EOD Tue.
- Vivek: draft the 4xGPU committed quote and a hosted ballpark (include amortized infra line items). I'll review and then we share with Luis. ETA Wed morning.
- Neha: package SOC 2 summary + one-pager on encryption and key management. Also include retention/audit log options for Velox’s security brief. ETA Wed COB.
- Marissa: draft a short proposal and acceptance criteria page (I own this). Will attach proposal-draft.docx to the HubSpot record.

Risks & mitigations
- If p95 > 150ms on initial hosted run, we should be ready to propose a short dedicated POC to show gains from colocated GPU pools and caching.
- Procurement timelines could stretch; if we can get a signature on a short pilot contract (2 weeks) that will buy runway.

I'll schedule a 30m triage on Thu to go over results — calendar invite to follow.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
